headline: Global Health Victories: HIV Down 40% Since 2010
meta_description: WHO's 2026 World Health Statistics show new HIV infections dropped 40% globally since 2010, alongside major gains in disease control and water access.
summary_short: New HIV infections have fallen 40% worldwide since 2010, according to WHO's latest World Health Statistics report, marking a major public health milestone.
body:
New HIV infections have fallen 40% worldwide since 2010, according to the WHO's World Health Statistics 2026. The milestone reflects decades of sustained effort in prevention, treatment, and care across the globe.

The progress extends beyond HIV. Neglected tropical disease needs have dropped 36%, freeing resources and reducing suffering in some of the world's most vulnerable populations. Simultaneously, billions more people have gained access to basic water and sanitation—a foundational step toward preventing infectious disease and improving quality of life.

These gains underscore what coordinated public health action can achieve. While challenges remain, the data shows that investment in disease prevention and basic infrastructure saves lives and creates the conditions for entire communities to thrive.
